messages:
maya: Heads up — after the mkdocs -> docusaurus migration I hit broken internal anchors on Windows builds. Repro steps below, seems related to backslashes in example paths and code fence slugify.

kevin: can you paste a minimal repro?

maya: repro:
```
# file: docs/setup/windows-paths.md
## Installing (C:\Program Files\redwood)

Link: [install steps](#installing-c:\program-files\redwood)
```
When the site builds, the anchor becomes `installing-c-program-files-redwood` locally but CI slugifies differently and linkcheck marks it broken.

alex: ok — two things: 1) backslashes should be normalized to forward slashes before slugify, 2) code fences with inline parentheses can create duplicate slugs if headings contain parens. Suggest adding a mkdocs plugin hook or use Docusaurus's heading id frontmatter.

sophie: also saw failures when headings include em-dash or non-ascii (e.g., “naïve”) — mkdocs' default slugify strips different chars than docusaurus. We should normalize slug pipeline (NFKC + remove punctuation) to avoid duplicate IDs. :warning:

deploy-bot: build #4123 failed — linkcheck found 23 broken internal links. See CI: https://ci.redwood/example/4123

kevin: i'll open a tiny patch that normalizes slugs and adds a unit test for Windows paths. want to include a test page with `C:\` example.

maya: please also add a docs-test for the linkcheck job and a snippet note in the migration guide. Minimal PR template:
- normalizer in docs-helpers
- unit test in docs-test
- migration note in migration.md

alex: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/789 — initial implementation, tests, and CI patch. please review.

sophie: nits: add a changelog entry and mention impacts to plugins consuming heading ids. also run linkcheck locally with `mkdocs build --strict` before merging.

maya: thanks — i'll review now. after merge run a new deploy and verify CI linkcheck count drops. :thumbsup:

kevin: merged and deployed to staging, linkcheck errors down to 1 (remaining is external redirect). closing.

maya: awesome, adding to migration checklist and emailing integrators. great teamwork!
